findings.detail: H1.2 ends at ER stress and H1.3 starts at DSP, so H1 is two arms (rs35705950 → MUC5B → ER stress, and DSP → EMT) that meet only in H1.4's compound subject; H1.1 → H1.2 connects only after merging 'MUC5B mucin' with 'ectopic MUC5B expression'.

H2.1 ends at telomere maintenance and H2.2 starts at short telomere length (only a GO-definition bridge joins them); H2.3 ends at ER stress and H2.4 starts at AT2 senescence, so the SFTPC arm never reaches IPF. No step leads into AT2 senescence at all (H2.2 goes from short telomeres straight to IPF), so the convergence on AT2 senescence that the title claims is never stated as a step.
H3.1 and H3.2 end at IRAK1 and aggrephagy, H3.3 starts at 'TOLLIP variants' and H3.4 at N-acetylcysteine, so the TOLLIP claim has no route to IPF.

H4.1 ends at RhoA activity, and H4.2 and H4.3 start at FAM13A variants; no step links RhoA to any lung outcome, though PMID:29066090 (cited at H4.2) says RhoA 'is known to be involved in profibrotic signalling pathways'.
H5.1 ends at IPF and H5.2 starts at 'independent epithelial lesions'; the two steps share no node.
H1's chain concludes at pulmonary fibrosis, not IPF, and its only tested evidence for that step is bleomycin fibrosis in mice.

Of the 44 citations on run steps (counted once per step), 24 do not state their step and 20 do (6 of those are Open Targets scores for H5.1's unsigned associations); 4 of the 24 state another step and were moved (PMID:18635891, PMID:23535734, PMID:29066090, PMID:42587125), and 2 supporting citations no step cites state a step.

No citation for H2.3 mentions misfolding or ER stress (a Reactome enrichment, the SFTPC UniProt entry, and an IPF ER-stress paper that does not name SFTPC); the run's own note says the step is not demonstrated.

The two single-cell papers cited for H2.4 show a senescence-like transitional AT2 state persists in fibrotic lungs, a disease feature rather than a cause, and nothing cited says failed alveolar regeneration causes IPF.
FAM13A → RhoA inhibition rests on a Rho-GAP domain annotation; the cited review says only 'modulation of Rho', so I13 has no evidence.

PMID:23583980 (cited for TOLLIP variants) does not name TOLLIP; PMID:29066090 and PMID:31710517 (cited for FAM13A variants) do not name FAM13A; PMID:23535734 (cited for short telomeres and IPF) reports TERT/TERC SNPs, not telomere length.
The PANTHER record says its NAC-alone comparison is not reported; what it does report (the NAC-containing combination raised death and hospitalisation) appears nowhere in the run.

H3's title says TOLLIP sets treatment response 'not baseline susceptibility', but its own cited GWAS reports TOLLIP variants associated with susceptibility (rs5743890 minor allele protective) as well as mortality (the same allele harmful).

The rs5743890 minor allele goes with lower IPF risk but higher mortality, and the GWAS says the TOLLIP minor alleles lower TOLLIP expression (20% for rs5743890, p=0.097); reduced TOLLIP fits the hypothesis for mortality and runs against it for risk, and BioLean can hold the two aspects only as two separate assoc statements.

The review cited for H4.1 says FAM13A is 'linked to mitigated fibrotic remodeling in PF', a protective direction the hypothesis never states, and calls FAM13A lung-enriched where the run's own HPA record shows no lung enrichment.

H4 calls FAM13A a Rho-GAP (a RhoA brake), and PMID:29066090, which it cites at H4.2, says RhoA activation is profibrotic and that the IPF risk allele at the RhoGEF AKAP13 raises AKAP13; with the review's 'mitigated fibrotic remodeling', the run's own texts point to FAM13A being protective, yet H4 gives FAM13A no direction ('sets the amplitude').

H1 places its one lesion in the distal airway (respiratory bronchiole) epithelium and says alveolar loss is not the driver, but its DSP-EMT evidence (PMID:42120512) is in alveolar epithelial cells, and its MUC5B paper (PMID:41091081) reports ectopic MUC5B in AT2 cells as well as bronchioles; the cited texts put the DSP arm in the alveolus, not the airway.
PMID:39418199, cited for H4.3, reports that MUC5B rs35705950 is not associated with a UIP pattern in SSc-ILD, a null for H1's variant outside IPF that the run does not use.

The run leaves these associations unsigned though the texts it cites give directions (shorter telomeres in IPF; rs5743890 protective for risk, harmful for mortality; rs2609255 OR 3.40 for UIP in SSc-ILD).

Every hypothesis's contradicting_evidence is prose about expression sites, STRING topology, constraint and missing records; none of the accessions it names refutes a chain step, and OT:MUC5B-constraint and OT:DSP-constraint are not in sources.json.

Supporting citations no step cites and that state no step: HPA:ENSG00000117983, HPA:ENSG00000096696, HPA:ENSG00000168484, HPA:ENSG00000078902, HPA:ENSG00000138640, HPA:ENSG00000164362, R-HSA-9825895, R-HSA-351906, OT:FAM13A-safety, STRING:SFTPC-MUC5B, STRING:TOLLIP-MUC5B, STRING:TERT-MUC5B, STRING:FAM13A-MUC5B. PMID:30345907 went to I1 and PMID:31900205 to I17.
P15924 (cited for H1.3) says DSP binds telomeric DNA and maintains telomere length via TRF2; the run raises it only as contradicting prose for H5, and no step links DSP to telomeres or to H2.
H5.1 reads distributively (each of six genes goes with IPF) and was split; at its own step each gene has only an Open Targets score, and the papers stating the associations are cited at other steps.
BLN:SFTPC-BRICHOS-mutation and BLN:FAM13A-variants are variant classes with no public identifier; the FAM13A one is the run's unspecified 'FAM13A variants'.

The guide's kind table has no row for an Open Targets association score; the unsigned gene-IPF statements keep theirs as observational. Recorded as curatedDb on a first pass, one OT score alone made 'FAM13A goes with IPF' established (belief 4/5).

Observational evidence weighs the same for an association as for an effect, so MUC5B-IPF, with two GWAS rows (p=2.5e-37, OR 2.89 at p=1e-66) and an Open Targets score, reaches only belief 3/4: an association claim cannot be established by the design that tests associations.
H1 says confidence medium; both arms compose but Lean finds them unsupported (belief 7/24 for rs35705950 and 1/4 for DSP, against pulmonary fibrosis rather than IPF).
H2 says confidence medium; the TERT arm rests on a GO-definition bridge and a discounted association (belief 16/175, unsupported) and the SFTPC claim has no route.

H5 says confidence medium for 'the set is not a module', but its only set-level records are STRING and Reactome enrichments, and the run's own cited UniProt text (DSP maintains telomere length) argues for a DSP-TERT link.

PMID:42120512's abstract reports the SYISL-DSP-YAP-EMT axis without saying whether it was shown in cells or mice, so neither inVitro nor mechanistic-with-taxon can be chosen from the span. v1's mechanistic with no taxon claimed a human in vivo perturbation, which the paper cannot have done; the audit records it as inVitro, the lower-weight of the two possible designs.
Allele dosage: the rs2609255 association is for two copies (recessive); a dbSNP entity names one allele, so the dosage sits only in the label.
A genotype-stratified drug response (NAC benefit confined to a TOLLIP genotype) could take a condition-refined subject, but the step has no sign and no record tests it, so it stays unexpressed.

An eQTL sentence ('the variant allele ... was associated with up-regulation in MUC5B expression') is kept as observational evidence for an effect, like v1's PMID:41091081; the line between observational evidence and the association_only exclusion is not drawn for a variant's effect on its own gene.
v1 excluded PMID:21506741 as not stating expression by genotype because the old fetch cut the text at 'P<0.001'; the re-fetched text states it, so it is now evidence for I1.
sources.json marks no citation cited_as 'contradicting' for this run, because the run's contradicting_evidence is prose; the accessions it names are fetched only when also cited elsewhere.
v1: H5.1's subject is a list of six genes. v2 splits it into six unsigned gene statements, and keeps only the set-level enrichment as set_valued.

Slash labels are ambiguous: 'AT2 senescence / failed alveolar regeneration' is split (the mechanism lists them separately), while 'IRAK1 phosphorylation / IL-1R-TLR signalling' stays one node, IRAK1 activity, because the UniProt text gives a direction only for IRAK1.

audit.reason: mechanistic with no taxon means an in vivo perturbation in the claim's organism (human), which this paper cannot have done. The span reports cell-level assays (DSP degradation, YAP1 nuclear translocation, histone marks at the vimentin locus) and the abstract's only in vivo work is SYISL knockdown in mice. inVitro is the lower-weight of the two possible designs. The DSP arm drops from belief 49/100 to 1/4 (still unsupported).

Same paper, same problem: the span ('promotes an EMT-associated state ... crosstalk contributes to pathological ECM deposition') states no design, and nothing in the abstract is a human in vivo perturbation. Its in vivo work (AAV-shSYISL, ASOs in mice) tests SYISL, not EMT.
